title: Oculibre: use your Android phone as a webcam, free and open source
description: Turn any Android phone, even an old one, into a webcam for Windows and Linux. Over encrypted Wi-Fi or USB, up to 1080p60 or 4K. Free, open source, no account.
og_title: Oculibre: your Android phone becomes your webcam
og_image_alt: The Oculibre window on a computer, showing a phone's camera live
hero_text: Oculibre turns any Android phone, even an old one, into a webcam for your computer. Over Wi-Fi or the USB cable, in every app, with no account and nothing sent to the cloud.
hero_img_alt: The Oculibre window on the computer: the phone's camera live in 1080p at 60 frames per second, with the latency, the camera and the quality settings
hero_phone_alt: The Oculibre app on the phone, live
features_intro: The camera of the phone sleeping in your drawer is better than most webcams. Oculibre puts it to work.
f1_text: Open source under the MIT licence. No ads, no watermark, no “Pro” tier, no time limit.
f2_text: The video goes straight from the phone to your computer, never through a server. Over Wi-Fi it is encrypted, and only a phone you paired can connect.
f3_text: Android 5.0 and up: a second life for a phone from 2015, and one less device thrown away.
f4_text: Up to 1080p at 60 frames per second, or 4K, with about 80 ms of delay. The computer decodes the video on its graphics card.
f5_text: The phone shows up as a webcam named “Oculibre” in OBS, Zoom, Teams, Discord, Google Meet, your browser and the Windows Camera app.
f6_text: Installers for Windows and Linux, no terminal needed. Every camera of the phone, chosen from the computer. Apps in English and French.
how_intro: The phone films and compresses the video with its own hardware. Oculibre on the computer decodes it, turns it the right way up and hands it to a virtual camera that every app sees as a real webcam.
how_img_alt: The phone films and encodes the video, sends it over Wi-Fi (encrypted, paired with a QR code) or the USB cable to the computer, which decodes it and shows it as the webcam Oculibre in every app
step1_text: Install Oculibre on the computer and on the phone.
step1_img_alt: The Oculibre app on the phone, ready: one Start button
step2_text: On the computer, click Add a phone and scan the QR code with the phone. Next time, the phone finds the computer by itself.
step2_img_alt: Pairing a phone with a QR code in the Oculibre window
step3_text: Press Start on the phone, then pick the camera “Oculibre” in your app.
step3_img_alt: Oculibre chosen as the camera in OBS Studio
usb_note: Over the USB cable: for now it needs USB debugging on the phone (Developer options), which gives the computer wide access to the phone: allow only your own computer. A version without it is planned. Wi-Fi does not need it.
download_intro: Oculibre is in beta. It works well on the computers and phones it was tested on, and your reports help it work on more.
dl_windows_note: Not signed yet: if Windows shows “Unknown publisher”, choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
dl_linux_note: Open the package with the software centre: it sets up the virtual camera, Secure Boot included. Other distributions: build from source.
dl_android_note: Allow installing apps from your browser or file manager when Android asks.
dl_macos: macOS: not yet, it is planned.
dl_checksums: Check a download with SHA256SUMS.txt. Every package is built from the public source by GitHub, from a version tag.
p1: No account, no server, no telemetry. Oculibre has nowhere to send your picture but your computer, and this site has no tracker or cookie either.
p2: Encrypted Wi-Fi. The video is protected with TLS, and the keys are exchanged by the QR code: nobody else on the network can watch the stream or inject a picture, and the computer only accepts the phones it paired.
p3: Works without the internet. The phone and the computer only need the same local network, or a cable.
p4: Open to inspection. All the code is public. Found a vulnerability? Report it privately.
signing_text: Free code signing on Windows will be provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation (application in progress; until then the Windows installer is unsigned). Packages are built by the public release workflow; only Oculibre's own programs are signed. Team roles and details: code signing policy.
privacy_statement: This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it.
a1: Yes. Oculibre is free and open source software under the MIT licence: no ads, no paid version, no watermark, no time limit.
a2: Any app that uses a webcam: OBS Studio, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Meet and other browser calls, the Windows Camera app… Choose the camera “Oculibre”. On Windows 11 a second one appears, “Oculibre” followed by “Windows Virtual Camera” in your language: it serves one app at a time, so pick the plain “Oculibre” to use several apps at once.
a3: Wi-Fi is the simplest: pair once with a QR code, and the video is encrypted. USB gives the steadiest picture, but for now it needs USB debugging turned on in the phone's developer options.
a4: Any Android phone from version 5.0 (2014) should work; the app only offers the modes your phone really delivers. It was tested on a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra and a Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro. Yours is not in the list? A device report helps a lot, old phones most of all.
q5: Why does Windows warn about an unknown publisher?
a5: The installer is not signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen does not know it. Choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”. Free signing through SignPath Foundation is being set up.
a6: Not yet: Oculibre is video only for now. A virtual microphone is planned for later.
a7: A macOS version is planned. The phone side is Android only.
footer_tagline: Free and open source webcam for Android phones.
